title: CRLR/549/2022 of SHANTANU AGARWAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 549 of 2022
Shantanu Agarwal ...........Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others .......... Respondents
Ms. Neetu Singh and Mr. Vinod Chandra, Advocates for the revisionist.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. with Ms. Sonika Khulbe, Brief Holder for the
State of Uttarakhand.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to the
order dated 03.08.2022, passed in Case No.194 of 2020,
Smt. Nishi vs. Shantanu, by the court of Judge, Family
Court, Haridwar, District Haridwar (for short, "the
case"). By the impugned order, an application for interim
maintenance, filed by the respondent no.2, Smt. Nishi
for herself and for her son, the respondent no.3,
Aaransh has been allowed and the revisionist has been
directed to pay `10,000/- to the respondent no.2, Smt.
Nishi and `5,000/- to the respondent no.3, Aaransh as
an interim maintenance to be paid from the date of filing
of the application.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.

2
3. The record reveals that the respondent
no.2 has filed an application seeking maintenance from
the revisionist under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973 (for short, "the Code") for herself and
her son, the respondent no.3. That is how the case was
instituted. In that case an application for interim
maintenance have been filed on the ground that after
marriage, the respondent no.2 was harassed and
tortured for the additional demand of dowry. She has
been staying separate from the revisionist. She is not
able to maintain herself whereas, the revisionist is a
person of means. This application was objected to by the
revisionist on the ground that the revisionist never
harassed or tortured or deserted his wife. The
respondent no.2, on her own, is staying separate.
Marriage is admitted. It is also admitted that the
respondent no.2 and the revisionist has a child.
4. In the case, the interim maintenance has
been allowed and the revisionist has been directed to
pay the interim maintenance, as stated hereinabove.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that, in fact, the revisionist is not a person of
such means, as determined by the court below. He is an
employee, who gets `8,200/- per month salary; he had

3
filed the pay certificate, which was not considered by the
court below while passing the impugned order.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
also submit that though the revisionist was earlier
running a company, but subsequently, it was closed.
The revisionist is ready and willing to keep his wife, the
respondent no.2 and his son, the respondent no.3 with
him. He is still ready to pay them interim maintenance.
But, it is argued that from the date of order, the interim
maintenance is huge, which the revisionist finds unable
to pay.
7. Reference has been made to some
telephonic conversation between the respondent no.2
and her brother-in-law, which is Annexure No.6 to this
revision. Some part of it, has been referred, to argue
that, in fact, the brother-in-law of the respondent no.2,
is the person, who is interfering in the marital life of the
revisionist and the respondent no.2. Learned counsel
would submit that it is a family matter. If the parties are
called, perhaps in the mediation, the matter may be
amicably settled and the family may be united.
8. It is also argued that while calling the
private respondents in the Court, the Court may direct
the revisionist to pay the arrears in installments.

4
9. This is a revision, the scope is quite
restricted to the extent of examining, legality, propriety
and correctness of the impugned judgment and order.
The impugned order is an order for interim maintenance.
The matter has to be finally decided after parties are
afforded an opportunity to adduce the evidence.
10. Impugned order reveals that, in fact, with
regard to income, the revisionist has raised arguments,
which have been deeply and extensively considered by
the court below. The court below has observed that, in
fact, on 01.06.2022, the revisionist was asked to give
details, as to how is he related to the Shaan Trading
Company. But, thereafter on 04.06.2022, the revisionist
got the GST registration cancelled which was in his
name. The court below observed that it reveals that the
revisionist was involved in the business of Shaan
Trading Company.
11. The court below also observed that, in fact,
admittedly the revisionist is paying `21,499/-
installment for some loan. If a person earns `8,200/-
how could he pay `21,499/- EMI? This aspect is also
been considered by the court below.
12. In so far as conversation is concerned,
which is Annexure No.6 to this revision, there are

5
various issues related to it. How could a husband
retrieve the telephonic conversation of his wife? A line
here and a line there in a conversation does not make
out any sense. There are other statements, which
perhaps may refer that the respondent no.2 had some
problems with her in-laws house.
13. Of course, the revisionist and the
respondent no.2 are in matrimonial discord. There is
some issues between them and it is also true that if
efforts for mediation is made, perhaps the parties may
arrive at an amicable settlement. But, only for that
purpose, it may not be in the interest of justice to call
private respondents in this Court. The matter is still
pending in the Family Court. This Court has no doubt
that the Family Court may also made all efforts so that
the parties may arrive at some amicable settlement. If
required, the matter may be referred to mediation.
14. Therefore, on merits, there is no reason to
interfere in this revision.
15. It has been argued that the respondent
no.2 be called in the Court and in the meantime, the
revisionist may be directed to pay the arrears of the
interim maintenance to the private respondents in
installments.

6
16. This Court has already held that there is
no purpose of calling private respondents in this Court
for the purpose of mediation, but in so far as payment of
arrears in instalments is concerned, definitely, this
aspect may require consideration.
17. Since, private respondents are not before
this Court, this Court refrains to make any order
permitting the revisionist to pay the arrears in
instalments. But, definitely, if such an application is
moved before the court below, there is no doubt that the
court below would consider it and may consider to
permit the revisionist to pay the arrears of the interim
maintenance in installments.
18. The revision stands disposed of
accordingly.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 21.09.2022
Sanjay
